basics.name: Joshua Sylvester
basics.label: Cyber Security Researcher
basics.summary: A motivated and hardworking researcher with a passion for artificial intelligence and cyber security. Experienced in reinforcement learning, cyber defence, and machine learning applications. Committed to advancing autonomous cyber defence through scalable reinforcement learning methods and the detection and mitigation of novel threats.

work.name: University of Kent
work.summary: Lead instructor during practical sessions, responsible for grading, feedback, academic support, and facilitating student engagement.
highlights: Prepared instructional materials and guided student projects.

work.name: Alan Turing Institute
work.summary: Researching reinforcement learning for autonomous cyber defence.

work.name: Orange Cyberdefense
work.summary: Applied machine learning to cybersecurity problems such as text classification and named-entity recognition. Automated data labelling and built containerised solutions for production.
highlights: Developed web scrapers and automated labelling pipelines.
Produced monthly and final-year security landscape reports.

education.summary: Working on autonomous cyber defence and reinforcement learning, with research published at IEEE CSR and collaboration with Dstl ARCD on 'Reward shaping for network defence based on reinforcement learning.'
Awarded for outstanding overall performance and best final-year project in the School of Computing.

awards.title: Best Student Paper Award
awards.awarder: 1st International Workshop on AI Safety and Security (AI-SS) - EDCC 2026
awards.summary: Received the Best Student Paper Award at the AI Safety and Security workshop for the paper 'Agentic Knowledge Distillation: Autonomous Training of Small Language Models for SMS Threat Detection'.

awards.title: Distinguished Paper Award
awards.summary: Received the Distinguished Paper Award at the AutonomousCyber 2025 workshop for outstanding research contribution to autonomous cyber defence.

awards.title: Outstanding Overall Performance in the School of Computing
awards.summary: Awarded to the highest performing student of the year for achieving the best overall marks in the degree programme.

awards.title: Best Final Year Computing Research Project award
awards.summary: Best Final Year Computing Research Project award, given to the student with the highest performing research project in the degree programme.

projects.name: Reward Shaping for Network Defence
projects.summary: Collaborative research project with Dstl ARCD exploring reinforcement learning techniques for autonomous cyber defence agents.
highlights: Applied reinforcement learning to network defence tasks.
